preview: Harshal Ubale shares his interview experience for an internship at Visa, detailing the online assessment coding round and the technical-cum-HR interview.
content: VISA Harshal Ubale TY Comps (2020 – 2024) VISA Experience Overview: This was the first time that VISA was coming to our campus, so it came as a bit of surprise to us and yeah it also got us a little excited for the company. So as there was no prior experience about the company in our archive, we had to do some digging for the company and the best place to do it was none another than GeeksforGeeks. So, I read all the archives from GFG and this was the summary 1. They had 2 Rounds in order to get an internship, first was Online Coding Round (Conventionally 2 DSA Problems will be given to solve in 1 hour), second round was mainly technical but they also ask a few HR Questions (the HR Questions are generally just to test how much excited are u for the company, so this a general tip: always show excitement/enthusiasm/confidence in HR Round). 2. They mainly ask Dynamic Programming, Graph, Backtracking, Heap and Recursion so to sum up, prepare DSA thoroughly. After reading all the articles, I contacted some of their previous interns from other colleges through Linkedin and they also fed me the same experience as above. In fact, one guy told me that his interviewer gave him four DSA questions to solve and said if u solve them then you are selected no further questions asked (but again it is not NECESSARY that it will happen to you too!!). 8th Sept 2022 – Pre-Placement Talk They held their PPT on Microsoft teams. Note down their Mission/Principles/Values/Vision cuz these are the things that you’ll be needing in HR Round. 9th Sept 2022 – First Round (Online Assessment) It was conducted on Hackerank where everyone was allotted a different pair of DSA problems and the time limit was an hour. We weren’t the only ones that were giving the test, but IIT Gandhinagar (as far as I remember) was also scheduled parallelly so the toughness of pool of those questions was from medium to hard. Tip: Try to solve any Online Assessment as soon as possible, if it contains only Coding Questions then it’s a big plus plus, but if the OA also contains MCQs then please don’t end up giving wrong answers in hurry. 1st Question Prefix XOR Given an Array where each element is XOR of all the previous elements in original array, return the original array. Now I don’t remember their sample examples but solution was somewhat similar to this vector<int> helper(vector<int> pref) { int n = pref.size(); vector<int> ans(n); ans[0] = pref[0]; for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) { ans[i]=pref[i]^pref[i-1]; } return ans; } Solution: a) A^ B = B ^ A b) A ^ A = 0 c) A ^ 0 = A pref[i] = arr [i] ^ arr[i - 1] ^ … arr [0] pref[i] = arr [i] ^ pref[i – 1] pref[i] ^ pref[i – 1] = arr [i] ^ pref[i – 1] ^ pref[i – 1] pref[i] ^ pref[i – 1] = arr [i] ^ 0 arr[i] = pref[i] ^ pref[i - 1] All test cases were passed. 2nd Question Team Formation The task was to form a team of size k from a given array by following below rules: a) You need to take two windows of size w from front and rear side of the array. b) Take the greatest score from the both windows and add it to the answer variable, at last delete the considered score from the array (so that it is not taken into consideration for next iteration). Solution: I used a max heap and added all the elements that were present in the window of size (w + k), from front and rear side of the array. Now I just needed to pop the max heap k times. int helper(vector<int> score, int k, int w) { int n = score.size(); priority_queue<int> q; int ans = 0; for (int i = 0; i < k + w; i++) { if (i < n) { q.push(score[i]); } } for (int i = n - k - w; i < n; i++) { if (i >= k + w) { q.push(score[i]); } } for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) { ans += q.top(); q.pop(); } return ans; } 10/14 test cases were passed and I submitted with 20 mins remaining on the clock. After this round, 10 students were shortlisted. 13th Sept – 2nd Round (Technical Round + HR Round for 1 hour) The Interviewer directly dived into my projects and started asking questions on them (no tell me about yourself questions were asked). Some of the general questions were: a) Motive for building the project? b) Reason for using this particular Tech Stack? For the project part, be prepared with everything such as Github, Online Database (if you are using any), etc. They may ask you to open it and present it in the meet. There were other questions also but they were specifically related to my project so they won’t help you much… So basically, we had conversation on my projects for almost 30 to 40 min and NO DSA questions were asked in the interview xD and because of this I had neutral feelings :/ cuz I was hoping at least a couple of DSA questions thrown in my way, but later it turned out that the interviewer was a project manager and was into managing teams and stuff so yup, this was kinda expected from a person at that position. Then she asked me a general question on how would you keep a record of the peoples who borrowed a book from a hypothetical library that you owned. I started designing a sql database for the situation and then there were some follow up questions on sql queries for the designed database. Then she asked a few questions on Core CS Subjects, they were on (I don’t remember most of them, but their toughness was on medium level): a) Deadlock b) How to prevent Deadlock c) Process, Threads (if you know java then you should also prepare multithreading) Then she moved onto HR part and asked these standard questions: a) Why Visa? b) One Moment in your life where you’ve done something extraordinary? Then she asked, what were the current technologies that I was learning to which I replied that, “currently I am not learning any new tech stuff but rather I was focusing on my DSA skills from a past few months, cuz you can learn new technologies within a couple of weeks (if given time) but before that you need to have a strong basic foundation for Computer Science and its core subjects”. Now this was the part which got her impressed xD and she replied positively with a smile :) Then she asked me if I had any questions, do ask questions, it shows your interest in their firm. Then she asked if I had any seniors who has experience as VISA interns. I told her that VISA came to our campus for the first time, to which she replied that it’s not possible because she had some members working on her team from VJTI and after some more chat we ended our meet. Now in my interview, no DSA questions were asked but you should be thoroughly prepared for DSA. Then at night, results came and they hired 4 interns and I was lucky enough to be one among them :) Resources: DSA: First of all, I prepared the basics through Abdul Bari’s Course of DSA on Udemy. Then I moved on to algorithms and started solving problems 1. I religiously solved leetcode’s problem of the day and solved TOP 100 Liked Questions. 2. I followed 450 DSA too. Operating System: I completed Gate Smasher’s playlist, studied notes of Apni Kaksha and also went through 40 Interview Bits Questions. 1. Gate Smashers 2. Apni Kaksha 3. Interview Bits 4. Operating System Frequently Asked Questions Difference between Semaphore and Mutex: 1. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 1 2. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 2 3. Difference between Semaphore and Mutex Part 3 DBMS: I completed Sachit Jains Playlist and went through Apni Kaksha Notes thoroughly (especially for queries) and then I went for Interview Bit’s notes: 1. Sanchit Jain 2. Apni Kaksha 3. Interview Bits Object Oriented Programming: I prepared OOP in my first year, so only some revision was needed on imp topics 1. Code With Harry (only if you have time) 2. Javapoint Tutorials (If you don’t have much time then this is the perfect source to study OOPs thoroughly) 3. Apni Kaksha 4. Interview Bits Computer Networks: 1. Apni Kaksha 2. Gate Smashers HR: Interview Bit Tips for Technical Round: 1. Smile. 2. Be Confident. 3. In any condition, don’t be silent, that puts a bad impression on the interviewer. 4. THINK OUT LOUD. 5. If offline, fill sheets with code/diagrams. 6. If online, use paint/tools. 7. Make it look like an interactive discussion. Tips for HR Round: 1. Smile. 2. Be Confident. 3. Prepare general questions. 4. Interview Bit. 5. Do some research about the firm.
